qe: What was the overarching administrative aim of the British policy-makers in India immediately following the post-war national scenario of 1946?
qh: 1946 के युद्धोत्तर राष्ट्रीय परिदृश्य के तुरंत बाद भारतीय शासन के संबंध में ब्रिटिश नीति-निर्माताओं का सर्वोपरि प्रशासनिक उद्देश्य क्या था?
o: A graceful withdrawal after a settlement on the modalities of the transfer of power
The complete, permanent dynamic expansion of direct imperial crown colonies
The immediate military suppression of all regional legislative assemblies
A total structural liquidation of the entire Indian Civil Service infrastructure
e: Detailed Explanation: By 1946, the British government realized that a settlement was necessary for burying the ghost of mass movements. The primary objective shifted entirely toward executing a graceful withdrawal after reaching an agreement on the modalities of the transfer of power and the nature of post-imperial India-Britain relations.

qe: On the eve of the Cabinet Mission’s arrival, what specific timeline sequence did the Congress demand regarding the settlement of minorities’ demands?
qh: कैबिनेट मिशन के आगमन की पूर्व संध्या पर, अल्पसंख्यकों की मांगों के निपटारे के संबंध में कांग्रेस ने किस विशिष्ट समय-सीमा के अनुक्रम की मांग की थी?
o: Minorities' demands must be worked out in an institutional framework only after the British left the country
The demands of the minorities had to be finalized before any transfer of central executive power could occur
A complete structural resolution enforced by a special three-judge panel of the High Court in London
The immediate and absolute implementation of a separate electorate blueprint before the war ended
e: Detailed Explanation: The Congress demanded that power be transferred to one central authority first. They maintained that minorities' demands should be worked out in a framework ranging from autonomy to self-determination, but strictly *only after* the British left.

qe: Why did the British administration structurally prefer a united and friendly India over partition in their 1946 strategic defense policy?
qh: ब्रिटिश प्रशासन ने अपने 1946 के रणनीतिक रक्षा नीति में विभाजन के बजाय एक संयुक्त और मित्रवत भारत को संरचनात्मक रूप से क्यों प्राथमिकता दी थी?
o: A divided India would lack in defense capability and would be a blot on Britain’s diplomacy
The princely states completely refused to award any seats to a partitioned union legislature
A united India was legally required to route 100% of its budget to the British Treasury
The separate communal electorates framework could only function within a single geographic list
e: Detailed Explanation: The British actively bid for a united and friendly India to serve as an active partner in the defense of the Commonwealth. They calculated that a divided India would lack sufficient defense capabilities and its creation would be viewed as a failure of British diplomacy.

qe: Which British Prime Minister delivered a historic speech on March 15, 1946, explicitly declaring that a minority cannot allow their veto to place a brake on the advance of the majority?
qh: किस ब्रिटिश प्रधानमंत्री ने 15 मार्च, 1946 को एक ऐतिहासिक भाषण दिया था, जिसमें स्पष्ट रूप से घोषित किया गया था कि एक अल्पसंख्यक को बहुसंख्यक वर्ग की प्रगति पर वीटो लगाने की अनुमति नहीं दी जा सकती?
o: Clement Attlee
Winston Churchill
Ramsay MacDonald
Stanley Baldwin
e: Detailed Explanation: In a sharp departure from earlier partisan policies, British Prime Minister Clement Attlee stated on March 15, 1946: '...though mindful of the rights of minorities... cannot allow a minority to place their veto on advance of the majority.'

qe: The high-powered Cabinet Mission arrived in Delhi on March 24, 1946. What were the two core issues designated for its prolonged discussions with Indian leaders?
qh: उच्च अधिकार प्राप्त कैबिनेट मिशन 24 मार्च, 1946 को दिल्ली पहुंचा। भारतीय नेताओं के साथ इसकी लंबी चर्चा के लिए कौन से दो मुख्य मुद्दे तय किए गए थे?
o: The formation of an interim government, and the principles and procedures for framing a new constitution
The immediate boundary demarcation of Pakistan, and the collection of wartime fiscal arrears
The complete administrative liquidation of Zila Courts, and enforcing English-medium education
The allocation of independent fiat currency printing licenses among different princely states
e: Detailed Explanation: The Cabinet Mission held extensive discussions with all major political parties and groups focused specifically on two crucial themes: (i) the formation of an interim government, and (ii) the principles and procedures for framing a new constitution giving freedom to India.

qe: Why did the Cabinet Mission Plan explicitly reject the Muslim League's demand for a full-fledged sovereign Pakistan in May 1946?
qh: कैबिनेट मिशन योजना ने मई 1946 में एक पूर्ण संप्रभु पाकिस्तान के लिए मुस्लिम लीग की मांग को स्पष्ट रूप से क्यों खारिज कर दिया था?
o: The proposed Pakistan would include massive non-Muslim populations (38% in the North-West and 48% in the North-East) and its formation would disrupt deep-seated regional ties
The central Legislative Assembly had passed an absolute resolution banning any geographic partition lists
The princely states refused to extend any financial credit inputs to support a separate Muslim nation
The project lacked any technical approval or clearance from the newly established Federal Court room
e: Detailed Explanation: The mission rejected a full-fledged Pakistan because it would contain vast non-Muslim minorities (38% in the North-West, 48% in the North-East). Furthermore, it would trigger the partition of Bengal and Punjab, disrupting deep-seated regional ties and creating severe economic, communication, and military problems.

qe: Under the structural grouping parameters of the Cabinet Mission Plan, which of the following regions constituted 'Section-B'?
qh: कैबिनेट मिशन योजना के संरचनात्मक समूहन (grouping) मापदंडों के तहत, निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा क्षेत्र 'सेक्शन-बी' (Section-B) के अंतर्गत आता था?
o: Punjab, North-West Frontier Province, and Sindh
Madras, Bombay, Central Provinces, United Provinces, Bihar, and Orissa
Bengal and Assam exclusively
The chief commissioner’s provinces combined solely with Burma
e: Detailed Explanation: The Cabinet Mission Plan systematically grouped the existing provincial assemblies into three sections. Section-B was structured to include the Muslim-majority northwestern provinces: Punjab, the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP), and Sindh.

qe: Which specific provinces were grouped together to form the high-population, Hindu-majority 'Section-A' under the 1946 Cabinet Mission Plan layout?
qh: 1946 की कैबिनेट मिशन योजना के खाके के तहत उच्च जनसंख्या वाले, हिंदू-बहुसंख्यक 'सेक्शन-ए' (Section-A) को बनाने के लिए किन विशिष्ट प्रांतों को एक साथ समूहित किया गया था?
o: Madras, Bombay, Central Provinces, United Provinces, Bihar, and Orissa
Punjab, North-West Frontier Province, and Sindh
Bengal, Assam, and the Chief Commissioner's administrative tracts
Bihar, Orissa, and Assam exclusively
e: Detailed Explanation: Section-A under the grouping system contained the core Hindu-majority provinces of British India: Madras, Bombay, Central Provinces, United Provinces, Bihar, and Orissa.

qe: According to the compositional blueprints of the proposed 389-member Constituent Assembly, exactly how many seats were allocated to be nominated by the native Princely States?
qh: प्रस्तावित 389 सदस्यीय संविधान सभा के संगठनात्मक खाके के अनुसार, देशी रियासतों (Princely States) द्वारा मनोनीत किए जाने के लिए सटीक रूप से कितनी सीटें आवंटित की गई थीं?
o: 93 members
292 members
4 members
52 members
e: Detailed Explanation: The Cabinet Mission Plan provided for a 389-member Constituent Assembly elected via proportional representation. Within this layout, British Indian provinces sent 292 members, chief commissioner's provinces sent 4, and the princely states were allocated exactly 93 members.

qe: What procedural sequencing did the Cabinet Mission Plan establish for formulating the respective provincial and union constitutions inside the Constituent Assembly?
qh: संविधान सभा के भीतर संबंधित प्रांतीय और संघीय संविधानों को तैयार करने के लिए कैबिनेट मिशन योजना ने कौन सा विशिष्ट प्रक्रियात्मक अनुक्रम स्थापित किया था?
o: Members from sections A, B, and C would sit separately to decide provincial constitutions first, then combine to formulate the union constitution
The entire assembly would sit together to finalize the union constitution before any provincial lists could be discussed
The princely states nominees held an absolute initial veto to dissolve the assembly sessions at will
All constitutional rules had to be verified and cleared by the provincial premiers prior to assembly voting
e: Detailed Explanation: Procedurally, members of groups A, B, and C were to sit separately first to decide the constitutions for their respective provinces and sections. Only after that phase would the entire combined assembly sit together to formulate the overarching Union constitution.

qe: Under the federal structure designed by the Cabinet Mission Plan, which specific subjects were to be controlled exclusively by a common centre?
qh: कैबिनेट मिशन योजना द्वारा तैयार किए गए संघीय ढांचे के तहत, किन विशिष्ट विषयों को एक साझा केंद्र (common centre) द्वारा विशेष रूप से नियंत्रित किया जाना था?
o: Defence, communication, and external affairs
Education, public health, and land revenue administration
Internal security, civil service rights, and judicial high courts
Currency valuation, agricultural credit lines, and local trade union lists
e: Detailed Explanation: The Plan envisaged a limited common center that would execute federal authority over three specific interconnected portfolios: defence, communication, and external affairs.

qe: How were controversial communal questions to be decided within the central legislature according to the 1946 Cabinet Mission guidelines?
qh: 1946 के कैबिनेट मिशन के दिशानिर्देशों के अनुसार केंद्रीय विधायिका के भीतर विवादास्पद सांप्रदायिक प्रश्नों का निर्णय कैसे किया जाना था?
o: By a simple majority of both communities present and voting
Through an absolute veto power granted exclusively to the Muslim League nominees
By referring the issue directly to a special three-judge panel of the High Court
According to the unilateral written certification issued by the central Governor-General
e: Detailed Explanation: To prevent majoritarian override on sensitive religious issues, the Plan stipulated that any communal question arising in the central legislature must be decided by a simple majority of both separate communities present and voting.

qe: What timeline indicator was provided by the Cabinet Mission Plan for a province to exercise its freedom to call for a reconsideration of the group or union constitution?
qh: कैबिनेट मिशन योजना द्वारा किसी प्रांत को समूह या संघ के संविधान पर पुनर्विचार करने का आह्वान करने की स्वतंत्रता का प्रयोग करने के लिए कौन सा विशिष्ट समय-सीमा संकेतक प्रदान किया गया था?
o: After 10 years
After the first six months of assembly sessions
Concurrent with the first annual budget presentation
Only after a flat period of twenty-five consecutive years
e: Detailed Explanation: The Plan provided a safety valve for provinces: after the execution of the first general elections, a province could choose to leave its assigned group, and after a duration of 10 years, it was free to call for a comprehensive reconsideration of the group or union constitution.

qe: How did the internal political interpretation of the 'grouping clause' differ fundamentally between the Congress and the Muslim League high commands?
qh: कांग्रेस और मुस्लिम लीग कमान के बीच 'समूहन खंड' (grouping clause) की आंतरिक राजनीतिक व्याख्या मौलिक रूप से किस प्रकार भिन्न थी?
o: Congress viewed grouping as optional, while the Muslim League believed Pakistan to be implied in compulsory grouping
Congress demanded compulsory structural grouping, while the League insisted on it being entirely optional
League argued that grouping required the immediate legal dissolution of the Constituent Assembly
Both held identical interpretations that grouping was a temporary tool to preserve British paramountcy
e: Detailed Explanation: The interpretation was split. The Congress believed that the plan rejected Pakistan because grouping was optional and a single constituent assembly was created. The League accepted the plan on the ground that it implied Pakistan through compulsory grouping (which the Mission later confirmed was compulsory).

qe: What primary organizational objection did the Congress lodge against the text composition of the proposed Constituent Assembly under the Cabinet Mission Plan?
qh: कैबिनेट मिशन योजना के तहत प्रस्तावित संविधान सभा के पाठ्य संगठन (text composition) के खिलाफ कांग्रेस ने कौन सा प्राथमिक संगठनात्मक विरोध दर्ज कराया था?
o: The absence of a provision for elected members from the princely states, as they could only be nominated by the princes
The inclusion of separate electorates based on the older Communal Award metrics
The mandatory restriction barring any vernacular-speaking delegates from entering the assembly
The statistical expansion of the house membership threshold up to 500 seats
e: Detailed Explanation: A major point of objection for the Congress was the non-democratic selection inside the princely states. The Plan contained no provision for elected representatives from the states, allowing them to be nominated exclusively by the autocratic princes.

qe: Viceroy Lord Wavell presented a specialized 'Breakdown Plan' to the Cabinet Mission in May 1946. What tactical operational course did this plan project?
qh: वायसराय लॉर्ड वेवेल ने मई 1946 में कैबिनेट मिशन के सामने एक विशेष 'ब्रेकडाउन प्लान' (Breakdown Plan) प्रस्तुत किया था। इस योजना ने किस रणनीतिक परिचालन मार्ग का अनुमान लगाया था?
o: The withdrawal of the British Army and officials to the Muslim provinces of the North-West and North-East, handing the rest to the Congress
The immediate and complete dynamic expansion of direct military rule across all provinces permanently
The absolute encapsulation of all Congress Working Committee leaders inside Yerwada jail
A complete synchronization of the British Indian Army with the Japanese frontline forces
e: Detailed Explanation: Wavell's Breakdown Plan visualised a middle course between 'repression' and 'scuttle'. It envisioned a strategic military withdrawal of the British Army and administrative officials exclusively to the Muslim-majority provinces of the North-West and North-East, leaving the rest of the country to the Congress.

qe: What did the subsequent formulation of Lord Wavell's Breakdown Plan reveal regarding high colonial official circles in May 1946?
qh: लॉर्ड वेवेल के ब्रेकडाउन प्लान के बाद के निरूपण ने मई 1946 में उच्च औपनिवेशिक आधिकारिक हलकों के संबंध में क्या प्रकट किया था?
o: British recognition of the impossibility of suppressing any future Congress-led rebellion and a desire to make a 'Northern Ireland' of Pakistan
A firm belief that the British administration possessed enough resources to crush mass movements indefinitely
The complete endorsement of the universal adult franchise metrics by the permanent civil bureaucracy
A calculated decision to permanently shift the imperial capital from Delhi back to Calcutta port
e: Detailed Explanation: Though superseded, Wavell's Breakdown Plan provided clear historical evidence of two factors: (i) the British recognition that it was impossible to suppress another massive Congress-led rebellion, and (ii) a desire among high official ranks to create a strategic 'Northern Ireland' out of Pakistan.

qe: On July 10, 1946, Jawaharlal Nehru delivered a provocative public statement regarding the sovereignty of the Constituent Assembly. What was his core assertion?
qh: 10 जुलाई, 1946 को जवाहरलाल नेहरू ने संविधान सभा की संप्रभुता के संबंध में एक उत्तेजक सार्वजनिक बयान दिया था। उनका मुख्य दावा क्या था?
o: That the Congress was not bound by a single thing except its decision to enter the Constituent Assembly, which would decide its own rules
That the Congress would fully endorse the compulsory grouping parameters inside sections B and C
That the entire assembly must be financially subordinated to the guidelines of the Chamber of Princes
That the rules of procedure were strictly dependent on the prior written clearance of Viceroy Wavell
e: Detailed Explanation: Nehru delivered a speech on July 10, 1946, stating: 'We are not bound by a single thing except that we have decided to go into the Constituent Assembly...' This implied the assembly was a sovereign body that would formulate its own rules, complicating the compulsory grouping agreements.

qe: How did the Muslim League react to Nehru’s provocative July 10 statement, permanently altering the course of the constitutional transition in July 1946?
qh: मुलाकात के बाद जुलाई 1946 में नेहरू के 10 जुलाई के उत्तेजक बयान पर मुस्लिम लीग ने कैसी प्रतिक्रिया दी, जिसने संवैधानिक संक्रमण के मार्ग को स्थायी रूप से बदल दिया?
o: The League withdrew its acceptance of the long-term plan and gave a call for 'direct action' from August 16 to achieve Pakistan
The League voluntarily dissolved its infrastructure to integrate fully with the Congress provincial cabinets
They petitioned the central legislative assembly to implement an immediate flat tax on Hindu zamindars
They signed a joint pact with the Sikh League to enforce universal adult franchise loop frameworks
e: Detailed Explanation: Infuriated by Nehru's speech, the Muslim League held a session on July 29, 1946, where they formally withdrew their previous acceptance of the Cabinet Mission's long-term plan. In retaliation, they issued a call for nationwide 'direct action' starting from August 16 to forcibly achieve Pakistan.

qe: A Congress-dominated Interim Government headed by Jawaharlal Nehru was sworn in on September 2, 1946. What strategic fear compelled the British to take this step?
qh: जवाहरलाल नेहरू के नेतृत्व में एक कांग्रेस-बहुल अंतरिम सरकार ने 2 सितंबर, 1946 को शपथ ली थी। किस रणनीतिक डर ने अंग्रेजों को यह कदम उठाने के लिए मजबूर किया था?
o: Fearing mass action by the Congress if the formation of government was delayed
The threat of an immediate economic blockade of coastal ports by British managing agencies
An absolute judicial injunction issued by the Chief Justice of the consolidated Federal Court
The physical threat of a synchronized mutiny breaking out inside the Royal Indian Navy ratings
e: Detailed Explanation: Fearing that any further administrative delay would prompt another massive, uncontrollable wave of mass action by the Congress, the colonial government quickly swore in the Congress-dominated Interim Government on September 2, 1946.

qe: Despite its transition title, how did the actual executive functioning of the 1946 Interim Government remain constrained, as illustrated by Wavell's actions in March 1947?
qh: अपने संक्रमणकालीन शीर्षक के बावजूद, 1946 की अंतरिम सरकार का वास्तविक कार्यकारी कामकाज कैसे सीमित रहा, जैसा कि मार्च 1947 में वेवेल के कार्यों द्वारा स्पष्ट होता है?
o: It was little more than a continuation of the old executive of the Viceroy, who famously overruled ministers on the release of INA prisoners
The popular Indian ministers held zero authority to assign portfolios or pass provincial tax laws
The entire cabinet framework was legally subordinated to the non-elected Chamber of Princes
Ministers were paid entirely out of personal donations realized from the Tilak Swaraj Fund savings
e: Detailed Explanation: Institutionally, the Interim Government was little more than a continuation of the old autocratic executive council of the Viceroy. This was made clear when Wavell used his overriding powers to overrule his ministers on the release of Indian National Army (INA) prisoners during his final cabinet assembly in March 1947.

qe: Viceroy Lord Wavell quietly brought the Muslim League into the Interim Government on October 26, 1946. Under what extraordinary political parameters was this entry permitted?
qh: वायसराय लॉर्ड वेवेल ने 26 अक्टूबर, 1946 को चुपचाप मुस्लिम लीग को अंतरिम सरकार में शामिल कर लिया। किस असाधारण राजनीतिक मापदंड के तहत इस प्रवेश की अनुमति दी गई थी?
o: The League joined without giving up 'direct action' and despite its rejection of both the long-term and short-term plans
The League was forced to formally surrender its demand for a separate Pakistan before entering the cabinet room
Jinnah had to sign a binding treaty pledging absolute structural compliance with Congress guidelines
The nominees were required to be chosen via competitive testing metrics managed by the general electorate
e: Detailed Explanation: Wavell brought the League into the government on October 26, 1946, as a political counterweight. In doing so, he compromised basic guidelines: the League was permitted to enter without renouncing its 'direct action' campaign and despite its explicit rejection of both the short-term and long-term Cabinet Mission plans.

qe: Who among the following leaders held the crucial portfolio of Finance inside the 14-member Interim Government cabinet between September 1946 and August 1947?
qh: निम्नलिखित नेताओं में से किसने सितंबर 1946 और अगस्त 1947 के बीच 14 सदस्यीय अंतरिम सरकार के मंत्रिमंडल के भीतर वित्त (Finance) का महत्वपूर्ण पोर्टफोलियो संभाला था?
o: Liaquat Ali Khan
Jawaharlal Nehru
Vallabhbhai Patel
Dr. John Mathai
e: Detailed Explanation: When the Muslim League integrated into the 14-member Interim Government cabinet, its prominent leader Liaquat Ali Khan was assigned the vital administrative portfolio of Finance.

qe: During the structural allocation of portfolios within the 1946 Interim Government, who was designated as the Minister of Labour?
qh: 1946 की अंतरिम सरकार के भीतर विभागों के संरचनात्मक आवंटन के दौरान, किसे श्रम मंत्री (Minister of Labour) के रूप में नामित किया गया था?
o: Jagjivan Ram
Rajendra Prasad
Asaf Ali
Jogendra Nath Mandal
e: Detailed Explanation: Within the 14 ministers of the Interim Government that functioned until August 15, 1947, the portfolio of Labour was held by the nationalist leader Jagjivan Ram.

qe: Which Muslim League nominee was assigned the portfolio of Law within the 14-member Interim Government framework?
qh: 14 सदस्यीय अंतरिम सरकार के ढांचे के भीतर किस मुस्लिम लीग के नामांकित व्यक्ति को कानून (Law) का पोर्टफोलियो सौंपा गया था?
o: Jogendra Nath Mandal
Ghaznafar Ali Khan
Ibrahim Ismail Chundrigar
Abdur Rab Nishtar
e: Detailed Explanation: To represent Dalit configurations aligned with their platform, the Muslim League nominated Jogendra Nath Mandal, who was assigned the portfolio of Law inside the Interim Government.

qe: In the historical evolution of the anti-Congress front, which Viceroy collaborated with Colvin in 1887 to launch a frontal attack on the Congress, propping up Syed Ahmed Khan?
qh: एंटी-कांग्रेस मोर्चे के ऐतिहासिक विकास में, किस वायसराय ने 1887 में कांग्रेस पर सीधा हमला करने के लिए कोल्विन के साथ सहयोग किया था, और सैयद अहमद खान को बढ़ावा दिया था?
o: Lord Dufferin
Lord Minto
Lord Curzon
Lord Irwin
e: Detailed Explanation: The containment policy against nationalism started early. In 1887, Viceroy Lord Dufferin alongside Colvin (Lt. Governor of UP) executed a frontal attack on the Congress and propped up conservative counters like Syed Ahmed Khan and Raja Shiv Prasad of Bhinga as an anti-Congress front.

qe: The 'Shimla Delegation' of October 1906 led by the Agha Khan met Viceroy Lord Minto to demand separate electorates. What specific justification did they offer for representation in excess of their numerical strength?
qh: अक्टूबर 1906 में आगा खान के नेतृत्व में 'शिमला प्रतिनिधिमंडल' ने अलग निर्वाचन क्षेत्र की मांग के लिए वायसराय लॉर्ड मिंटो से मुलाकात की थी। उन्होंने अपनी सांख्यिकीय संख्या से अधिक प्रतिनिधित्व के लिए क्या विशिष्ट औचित्य दिया था?
o: Their political importance and their contribution to the British Empire
Their exclusive mastery over the maritime transport routes crossing the western coast
The total absolute acreage of agricultural lands they managed under the Permanent Settlement
Their unique capacity to compile legal codes in English characters for the legislative councils
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1906 Shimla delegation argued that Muslim representation should be commensurate not merely with their baseline numeric strength, but explicitly with their 'political importance and their contribution to the British Empire'.

qe: Which group of aristocratic leaders founded the All India Muslim League in December 1906 to preach loyalty to the British government and isolate the Muslim intelligentsia from the Congress?
qh: दिसंबर 1906 में किन कुलीन नेताओं के समूह ने ब्रिटिश सरकार के प्रति निष्ठा का उपदेश देने और मुस्लिम बुद्धिजीवियों को कांग्रेस से अलग रखने के लिए अखिल भारतीय मुस्लिम लीग की स्थापना की थी?
o: The Agha Khan, Nawab Salimullah of Dacca, Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk, and Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk
Syed Ahmed Khan and Raja Shiv Prasad of Bhinga exclusively
Badruddin Tyabji, Mir Musharraf Hussain, and Hamid Ali Khan
U.N. Mukherji, Lal Chand, and the Maharaja of Kasim Bazar
e: Detailed Explanation: The Muslim League was institutionalized in December 1906 by conservative elites including the Agha Khan, Nawab Salimullah of Dacca, Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk, and Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk to ensure political loyalty to the Crown.

qe: In the history of communal polarization during the 1920s, which retaliatory movements were started by Muslim groups to counter the Hindu Shuddhi and Sangathan campaigns?
qh: 1920 के दशक के दौरान सांप्रदायिक ध्रुवीकरण के इतिहास में, हिंदू शुद्धि और संगठन अभियानों का मुकाबला करने के लिए मुस्लिम समूहों द्वारा कौन से प्रतिशोधात्मक आंदोलन शुरू किए गए थे?
o: Tabligh and Tanzeem movements
Faraizi and Wahabi insurrections
Aligarh and Deoband school loops
Karachi and Dacca direct action councils
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1920s saw severe communal friction. In response to the Arya Samajist Shuddhi (purification) and Sangathan (organization) movements aimed at reconverting populations, Muslim communal groups retaliated by launching the Tabligh and Tanzeem movements.

qe: Nationalist analysts note that the Congress committed a series of mistakes by negotiating with the Muslim League over constitutional reforms like the Nehru Report in 1928. Which of the following highlights one of these analytical mistakes?
qh: राष्ट्रवादी विश्लेषकों का मानना है कि कांग्रेस ने 1928 में नेहरू रिपोर्ट जैसे संवैधानिक सुधारों पर मुस्लिम लीग के साथ बातचीत करके कई गलतियाँ कीं। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा इन विश्लेषणात्मक गलतियों में से एक को रेखांकित करता है?
o: It gave legitimacy to the politics of the League, recognized the division of society into separate communities with separate interests, and undermined secular, nationalist Muslims
It forced the complete structural dissolution of the Congress Working Committee network permanently
It legally compelled the lower Federal Assembly to adopt a unicameral composition layout
It required all future national agitations to be funded by foreign managing agencies directly
e: Detailed Explanation: By entering into compromises on a communal baseline, the Congress gave political legitimacy to the League's divisive narratives, implicitly recognized that society was divided into separate communities with separate interests, and severely undermined the position of secular, nationalist Muslims.

qe: When did the shift occur from liberal communalism—centered around safeguards and reservations—to extreme communalism organized as a mass movement based on fear and hatred?
qh: सुरक्षा उपायों और आरक्षणों के इर्द-गिर्द केंद्रित उदारवादी सांप्रदायिकता से, भय और घृणा पर आधारित जन आंदोलन के रूप में संगठित चरम सांप्रदायिकता में बदलाव कब हुआ था?
o: After the 1937 provincial elections, following the poor performance of the Muslim League
Immediately after the formal declaration of the Morley-Minto reforms in 1909
Following the sudden suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement in August 1920
During the constitutional compilation of the Nehru Report parameters in August 1928
e: Detailed Explanation: Prior to 1937, liberal communalism predominated. However, after the Muslim League performed poorly in the 1937 provincial elections, it abandoned constitutional bargaining and shifted to extreme communalism, mobilizing the middle and upper classes via fear, hatred, and aggressive propaganda.

qe: Between 1937 and 1939, Mohammad Ali Jinnah effectively blocked all avenues for political conciliation by forwarding which impossible prerequisite demand to the Congress?
qh: 1937 और 1939 के बीच, मोहम्मद अली जिन्ना ने कांग्रेस के सामने कौन सी असंभव पूर्व-शर्त मांग रखकर राजनीतिक सुलह के सभी रास्तों को प्रभावी रूप से बंद कर दिया था?
o: That the Congress must declare itself a Hindu organisation and recognise the Muslim League as the sole representative of Indian Muslims
That the Congress must completely dissolve its central working committee infrastructure inside Wardha
The immediate and complete absolute termination of any ongoing anti-imperialist campaigns across provinces
That the party must adopt English characters exclusively as its sole communication medium internally
e: Detailed Explanation: Jinnah stalled all negotiations between 1937 and 1939 by raising an extreme prerequisite: he demanded that the secular Indian National Congress must formally declare itself a purely Hindu body and explicitly recognize the Muslim League as the single, exclusive representative of all Indian Muslims.

qe: On March 24, 1940, the historic 'Pakistan Resolution' was formally passed by the Muslim League. In which annual session did this landmark development occur?
qh: 24 मार्च, 1940 को मुस्लिम लीग द्वारा ऐतिहासिक 'पाकिस्तान प्रस्ताव' (Pakistan Resolution) आधिकारिक रूप से पारित किया गया था। यह ऐतिहासिक विकास किस वार्षिक सत्र में हुआ था?
o: The Lahore session
The Calcutta session
The Simla deputation assembly
The Karachi conference
e: Detailed Explanation: The formal demand for partition was institutionalized on March 24, 1940, when the Muslim League passed the historic 'Pakistan Resolution' during its annual session convened at Lahore.

qe: What structural privilege granted by the British India Government during the Second World War allowed the Muslim League to consistently stick to its demand for a separate Pakistan throughout all negotiations?
qh: द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के दौरान ब्रिटिश भारत सरकार द्वारा दिए गए किस संरचनात्मक विशेषाधिकार ने मुस्लिम लीग को सभी वार्ताओं में एक अलग पाकिस्तान की अपनी मांग पर लगातार टिके रहने की अनुमति दी?
o: The government gave a virtual veto to the League on any future political settlement
The state granted the League absolute control over 100% of the provincial list revenues
The direct judicial appointment of Jinnah as the permanent head of the executive council
Providing unlimited capital grant subsidies to fund the direct action volunteer corps
e: Detailed Explanation: During the war years, the British administration used the League to counter the Congress's anti-colonial campaigns by granting the League a virtual veto over any future political or constitutional settlement. The League fully leveraged this veto to stall the August Offer, Cripps proposals, Shimla Conference, and Cabinet Mission Plan.

qe: A logistic supply tracking pathway charts a precise right-angled triangular layout. A delivery car moves 24 km North from central yard O, and then changes orientations to drive 7 km East to reach storage spot B. Find the absolute straight-line distance from O to B.
qh: एक वाहन जंक्शन O से 24 किमी उत्तर की ओर चलता है, और फिर दिशा बदलकर पूर्व की ओर 7 किमी जाकर बिंदु B पर पहुँचता है। O से B की सीधी रेखा की दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए।
o: 25 km
31 km
28 km
30 km
e:
Detailed Explanation: This spatial path sets up a classic right-angled triangle with perpendicular legs of 24 km and 7 km. The straight-line distance is the hypotenuse.
By applying the Pythagoras theorem: $\text{Distance} = \sqrt{24^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{576 + 49} = \sqrt{625} = \mathbf{25\text{ km}}$.

qe: In a biological ecosystem study tracking energy metrics, if the Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of an alluvial marsh tract is measured at 46,000 units and the energy spent during metabolic plant respiration (R) accumulates to 14,000 units, calculate the Gross Primary Productivity (GPP).
qh: एक पारिस्थितिकी उत्पादकता सर्वेक्षण में, यदि एक मैदानी क्षेत्र की शुद्ध प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (NPP) 46,000 इकाइयाँ है और पौधों के श्वसन (R) के दौरान खर्च की गई ऊर्जा 14,000 इकाइयाँ है, तो सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (GPP) की गणना करें।
o: 60,000 units
32,000 units
48,000 units
54,000 units
e:
Detailed Explanation: Utilizing the foundational ecological productivity equation: $NPP = GPP - R$, we isolate Gross Primary Productivity: $GPP = NPP + R$.
Substituting the values: $GPP = 46,000 + 14,000 = \mathbf{60,000\text{ units}}$.

qe: Under the system of Dyarchy introduced by the Government of India Act 1919 at the provincial level, which of the following subjects was kept under the 'Reserved' list, managed directly by the Governor's bureaucratic executive council?
qh: प्रांतीय स्तर पर भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919 द्वारा शुरू की गई द्वैध शासन व्यवस्था के तहत, निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा विषय 'आरक्षित' (Reserved) सूची के तहत रखा गया था, जिसका प्रबंधन सीधे राज्यपाल की नौकरशाही कार्यकारी परिषद द्वारा किया जाता था?
o: Law and order, finance, land revenue, and irrigation
Education, public health, local self-government, and agriculture
Vernacular media publication, registration procedures, and library management
The corporate financing of swadeshi textile mills and indigenous shops
e: Detailed Explanation: Dyarchy divided provincial portfolios into two bands. Crucial administrative and financial subjects—such as law and order, public finance, land revenue, justice, and irrigation—were kept under the 'Reserved' list, managed directly by the Governor and his council of bureaucrats without accountability to the legislature.

qe: What macro-level transformation occurred to India's dynamic share of global manufacturing exports across the centuries of British colonial rule?
qh: ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक शासन के सदियों के दौरान वैश्विक विनिर्माण निर्यात (world manufacturing exports) में भारत कीं गतिशील हिस्सेदारी में बड़े पैमाने पर क्या परिवर्तन आया?
o: It dramatically fell from 27 per cent down to a mere 2 per cent
It increased steadily from 2 per cent up to an optimized 27 per cent
It remained perfectly constant at a balanced 10 per cent layout
It dropped to zero instantly within the first decade of the Charter Act of 1813
e: Detailed Explanation: As highlighted by modern economic historians, the systemic deindustrialization and forced commercialization under British rule caused India's share of world manufacturing exports to crash from a dominant 27 per cent down to a mere 2 per cent by the end of the colonial era.

qe: The judicial framework of the Cornwallis Code of 1793 established a major milestone in modern Indian administrative history by firmly introducing which concept?
qh: 1793 के 'कॉर्नवॉलिस कोड' ने किस प्रमुख अवधारणा कों दृढ़ता से पेश करके आधुनिक भारतीय प्रशासनिक इतिहास में एक बुनियादी मील का पत्थर स्थापित किया?
o: The principle of the sovereignty of law and the separation of revenue and justice administration
The absolute legal immunity of all colonial government officials from civil court oversight
The mandatory use of English instead of vernacular languages across all local lower subdivisions
The total structural centralization of all judicial functions under the district Collector
e: Detailed Explanation: The Cornwallis Code of 1793 was a landmark because it established the sovereignty of law and the separation of powers. It separated revenue administration from justice, divested the Collector of judicial duties, and made government officials answerable to civil courts for official actions.

qe: What retrogressive evaluation did the Simon Commission outline in its May 1930 report regarding the efficiency and financial management of local self-governing bodies since 1919?
qh: साइमन कमीशन ने मई 1930 की अपनी रिपोर्ट में 1919 के बाद से स्थानीय स्वशासी निकायों के कुशल और वित्तीय प्रबंधन के संबंध में कौन सा प्रतिगामी (retrogressive) मूल्यांकन प्रस्तुत किया था?
o: It claimed that the management of finances had deteriorated, and suggested the retrograde step of increasing provincial bureaucratic control over local bodies
It celebrated the village panchayats for successfully achieving absolute financial independence across all provinces
It demanded that 100% of local tax revenues must be channeled directly to support the All India Kisan Sabha
The Commission recommended the complete permanent legal abolition of the office of the district magistrate
e: Detailed Explanation: The Simon Commission (May 1930) noted that the financial management of local bodies had deteriorated since the introduction of the 1919 reforms, pointing out a lack of progress in village panchayats. Instead of expanding democracy, it recommended a retrograde step: increasing tight provincial bureaucratic control over these local bodies in the name of efficiency.
